<pasted_content id="85e7">
You are validating a hackathon solution for the BMW "AI for Product Decision Making" challenge.
Repo: /Users/atahankilic/Documents/ehl-munich-final. Act as a critical BMW judge + QA engineer:
verify that the solution actually meets the challenge, find gaps/bugs, and report them with evidence.
Do not rebuild things; fix only clear bugs, and ask before anything costly or architectural.

## What the challenge asks (read foundation/documents/challenge-brief.md for the full text)
Build an AI app that helps BMW product managers (PMs) derive, justify and prioritize CUSTOMER requirements
for a successor vehicle (3–5 yr horizon), from customer verbatims, BMW product/sales data and web research,
with the PM in control and a complete audit trail. Vehicles: 1 Series F70, 5 Series G60 (+China LWB G68),
7 Series G70; markets EU/US/CN. Minimum: one derivative in one market, but not a one-off.
Deliverables: (1) concept + working prototype, (2) structured requirement list — each with unique ID,
actionable description, linked findings and sources, priority/score, prioritization rationale, evidence
level, future-facing assumptions & uncertainties, decision status, (3) end-to-end workflow showing what AI
does autonomously vs. where human review is mandatory, (4) audit trail from sources → findings →
consolidation → scoring → prioritization → human decision (who/what, when, rationale; content, score,
priority, evidence, status changes; also access events).
In scope: features, equipment, comfort, space, usability, infotainment/digital, design & quality perception,
driving experience, range/charging as experienced, variants/packages. Out of scope: regulatory/homologation,
engineering/component specs/architecture, pricing/business case (rough effort as a factor is OK).
BMW mentors added: markets differ by climate/usage/culture; derive FUTURE needs; the process is ~2 years of
continuous re-prioritization, not a one-shot list.

## Mandatory first reads (project rules)
AGENTS.md (rules: raw BMW data in "challange information document/" is confidential and may only be sent to
OpenAI — never print raw verbatim text into your own context, use aggregate queries; AI only proposes, PM
decides; append-only audit; $100 OpenAI budget), then foundation/STATE.md, foundation/DECISIONS.md index
(D-024–D-033 are the latest session's decisions), foundation/OPEN_QUESTIONS.md, README.md.

## What was built (all committed on main, commits 7bd8f1b..f8166c5)
Stack: Python 3.12/uv, OpenAI only (gpt-6-luna bulk, gpt-6.1-sol reasoning, text-embedding-3-small),
SQLite data/app.db + sqlite-vec, LangGraph for wave orchestration (no LangChain), Streamlit UI. Every LLM
call goes through the budget-guarded wrapper src/bmw_req/llm/client.py (reserve → settle, logged in
llm_usage, identical calls cached in llm_cache, Flex→standard fallback).
Pipeline (src/bmw_req/):
- ingest/: feedback (10,128 verbatims), study.py (391 items, z-scores per model×market column),
  sales.py, options.py (458 option-list items from German PDFs, every line verified), reference.py +
  reference_data.py (platforms, plants, production, 21 competitor models, market profiles, BMW brand
  guardrails — status "proposed, PM sign-off needed"; 96 cited reference sources).
- research/: web research agents (luna + web_search); evidence kept only if its URL is in the response's
  citations; quotes verified by fetching where possible; 219 web items (T1/T2/T3), 152 web findings.
- pipeline/extract.py (extract-v3, D-024): 15,630 signals; support-call questions flagged, weighted 0.5.
- pipeline/findings.py (D-025): embeddings + agglomerative clustering (threshold 0.35) → verbatim findings
  G60 243 / F70 166 / G70 242 with per-market, per-wave metrics; study_findings.py → 391 study findings.
- pipeline/requirements.py (derive-v6, sol): per vehicle line, incremental; validates cited finding IDs and
  targets; consolidate() merges same needs across lines into portfolio requirements.
- pipeline/linker.py: attaches study items/web findings per target market (supports/contradicts/context).
- pipeline/fit.py: brand/segment/market/feasibility per target; brand FAIL blocks approval unless PM
  override; feasibility is non-blocking context (D-030).
- pipeline/scoring.py (score-v2, D-029): per derivative×market score = weighted factors (customer voice 30,
  satisfaction gap 15, market volume 15, competitive pressure 15, future relevance 15, portfolio leverage 10),
  renormalized over factors WITH data (missing data shown as evidence gap), × confidence by evidence level
  E1–E4, + market-fit and effort modifiers; empirical-Bayes shrinkage for small markets; bands Must ≥60,
  Should ≥45. Runs are snapshotted; a PM-confirmed priority that a later run would change → change_proposal
  with factor-level cause.
- pipeline/waves.py + graph.py (D-027): SIMULATED ingest waves (no dates in data): wave 1 = half the
  verbatims + 2024 sales + baseline web; wave 2 = other half + customer study + 2025/2030 sales; wave 3 =
  web "market event". LangGraph: open_wave → derive → link_evidence → fit_checks → prioritize.
- pipeline/challenge.py: PM challenges a requirement; sol answers using linked evidence + sqlite-vec
  semantic search over signals (the only RAG part); its edits become change proposals, never direct edits.
- service.py: the only write path for PM actions (rationale + named actor mandatory, audit events, access
  events, export_requirements()).
UI: app.py + ui/*.py — 11 pages: Overview (workflow AI vs human gates, funnel), Portfolio, Backlog,
Requirement (overview with EVIDENCE/ASSUMPTION/UNCERTAINTY/CONFLICT, score breakdown + history, evidence
chain graph, fit checks, PM decision incl. challenge, audit trail), Change inbox, Market conflicts, Findings
explorer, Weights & runs, Audit trail, Export, Budget.

## Current data state (DB = snapshot "demo")
53 requirements, 165 targets, 3 prioritization runs, 1,632 audit events, change proposals open/accepted/
rejected. PM decisions in this state are SCRIPTED (scripts/demo_build.py, rationales tagged
"[scripted demo decision]"). Snapshots in data/snapshots: evidence, wave1 (no PM decisions, for a live
demo), demo. Manage with `uv run python scripts/demo_state.py list|save|restore <name>` (stop Streamlit
first; restore keeps llm_usage/llm_cache). Export: data/exports/requirements_demo.json.
Spend: $6.86 of $100 (includes a $1.00 reconciliation row for usage rows lost in a since-fixed restore bug).

## How to run / check
uv run pytest -q (44 tests, no paid calls)
uv run streamlit run app.py  (http://localhost:8501; may already be running — check port 8501)
Benchmarks (results in data/eval/): scripts/benchmark_extraction.py (vs BMW labels, aggregates only),
scripts/benchmark_requirements.py [--judge] (deterministic checks + sol judge; last: judge 4.02/5, top-20
pain coverage 0.65–0.75), scripts/benchmark_scoring.py (rank stability under ±25 % weight noise; Kendall
tau 0.93–0.96).

## Known weak spots to examine
- Judge dimensions "measurable" (~3.5) and "evidence-grounded" (~3.6) are weakest.
- Wave 3 still adds ~11 requirements, some thinly evidenced (e.g. single-verbatim ones).
- Consolidation can miss duplicates; check for near-duplicate requirements.
- CN targets have no verbatims (study + web only) — check that this is shown honestly, not hidden.
- "Opening a wave" and "Challenge" block the UI while running (minutes); they cost money.
- Brand guardrails and reference facts are proposed, not yet PM-signed-off.
- Clusters were computed on all data, then shown per wave (a documented simulation shortcut).
- Self-judging: the judge is the same model family (sol) as the derivation model.

## Your validation task
1. Map every BMW deliverable and "app must be able to" item to concrete evidence in the app/DB
   (page, table, query). Produce a pass / partial / fail checklist with proof.
2. Trace 3 requirements end to end (one G60×US, one G68×CN, one portfolio requirement spanning lines):
   sources → findings → requirement → score breakdown → fit checks → PM decisions → audit events.
   Verify citations exist and support the claims (use aggregates/IDs and AI-written summaries; don't dump
   raw verbatims into your context).
3. Scope check: any requirement that is regulatory, engineering-spec or pricing? Any brand-fit misses?
4. Check AI-vs-human rule: no AI-made status/priority changes; every human action has actor + rationale;
   audit_event is append-only (triggers).
5. Click through the UI (Streamlit AppTest or browser) on snapshot "wave1" doing a live PM flow: confirm
   priorities, approve, reject, edit, override gate, challenge (costs ~$0.04), open wave 2 (~$0.5) and
   check the change inbox. Restore the snapshot afterwards.
6. Report: ranked findings (bugs, gaps vs brief, demo risks), each with evidence and a suggested fix;
   update foundation/STATE.md (session log) and log any decision/question per AGENTS.md. Do not commit
   unless asked.
</pasted_content id="85e7">

input.command: cat foundation/STATE.md && sed -n '1,80p' foundation/OPEN_QUESTIONS.md && sed -n '1,60p' foundation/DECISIONS.md && ls; lsof -i :8501 | head -3

## Minimal demo path (decided, D-021)

One thin slice end-to-end before anything else (AGENTS rule 18). It covers BMW's minimum of one derivative in one market (`challenge-brief.md`).
- **Scope:** 5 Series (D-005).
  - **G60 × US:** ~3.6k verbatims + detailed study + sales. Best-evidenced.
  - **G68 × CN:** study + sales, no verbatims, so web evidence and the market conflict carry it (D-011).

- **Flow:**
  1. Classify the G60 verbatims.
  2. Group them into findings with sources.
  3. Derive ~10–15 requirements with targets US/CN.
  4. Run fit checks.
  5. Score and explain.
  6. PM approves, rejects or challenges a few.
  7. Show the audit trail.
  8. Run wave 2 (Q-012) and show priority changes + change proposals.
- F70/G70 stay supported by the data model and run later through the same pipeline.

## Done

- Challenge analyzed; all BMW data profiled and re-verified (`documents/data-inventory.md`).
- Foundation, `AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md` created.
- BMW mentor input recorded (D-011 markets differ, D-012 future needs, D-013 continuous re-prioritization). BMW support recommended the annual report → `documents/bmw-annual-report-2025.md`.
- Model tiering (D-010); budget re-baselined (D-014).
- Q-001/002/003 answered by Atahan → D-005 (portfolio-level, 5 Series deepest), D-006 (OpenAI), D-007 (web knowledge base), D-008 (brand fit gate), D-009 (plant/platform feasibility).
- Conceptual architecture, requirement model and knowledge-base design drafted. Tech stack decided 2026-10-10 (D-015–D-020).
- Web research seeds written and fact-checked:
  - `portfolio-reference.md`: platforms, 14 vehicle plants + 3 CKD sites, BMW sales 2024–H1 2026, primary-sourced from the annual report where possible.
  - `competitor-landscape.md`: competitors, trends, expectations, brand-fit guardrails.
- Foundation review (2026-10-10) fixed, except the confidentiality items, which Atahan dropped.

## In progress

- Nothing.

## Demo (how to run)

- `uv run streamlit run app.py`. DB holds the full `demo` state; `uv run python scripts/demo_state.py restore wave1` for a live PM review from scratch (stop the app first). Rebuild: `scripts/demo_build.py`.
- Story: Overview (workflow, funnel) → Portfolio → Backlog G60×US / G68×CN / G60×EU → Requirement REQ-0001 (evidence vs assumption, score breakdown, evidence chain, fit, decision, audit) → Change inbox (wave 2/3 proposals) → Market conflicts → Weights & runs (re-rank live, free) → Audit trail → Export.

## Next up (suggested order)

0. Fill in Team & logistics (Q-007, Q-008); rehearse the demo path above.
1. Ask BMW mentors: Q-005, Q-006, Q-015, Q-016 (Q-010 is now decided as non-blocking, D-030 — confirm).
2. PM sign-off of the proposed brand guardrails (D-031) — they gate approval.
3. Quality levers (benchmarks in `data/eval/`): judge "measurable" (3.5) and "evidence-grounded" (3.6) are the weakest dimensions; top-20 pain coverage 65–75% after wave 1 (rest picked up in waves 2/3).
4. Optional: async/background wave runs in the UI (currently blocking), wave-3 derivation cap (it still adds ~11 requirements).

## Budget (OpenAI, $100 total — plan in D-014)

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Spent to date | **$6.86** (2026-10-10): derivation $2.38 (incl. prompt iterations v2–v6, 4 wave-1 runs, waves 2–3 ×2), web research $1.69, fit checks $0.55, extraction $0.52, linker $0.23, recheck $0.13, benchmarks $0.09, challenge $0.08, consolidation $0.08, other $0.12, **plus a $1.00 reconciliation row** (usage rows lost in a failed demo restore, upper-bound estimate; bug fixed). Source of truth: `llm_usage` / Budget page |
| Planned build spend | ≈ $60 (≈ $48 + 25% contingency) |
| Warn / block non-demo / app hard stop | $45 / $70 / $90 |
| Demo-day reserve | $20 ($70 → $90) |
| OpenAI project hard limit | $95 (to set by Atahan, + $45 alert) |

## Pilot results (2026-10-10, `scripts/pilot.py`, outputs in `data/pilot/`)

| Step | Calls | Tokens in / out (reasoning) | Cost | Latency (Flex) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Extract 50 G60 US verbatims (B 20, A/C/D 10 each, seed 42), luna low | 2 × 25 | 3.0k / 3.2k (452); 2.3k / 2.6k (142) | $0.0018 | 84 s, 66 s |
| Derive 5 requirements from 73 signals, sol medium | 1 | 6.1k / 2.1k (279) | $0.0183 | 35 s |

- **Extraction:** every ID returned, none invented, none duplicated; 73 signals; 1 verbatim correctly out of scope ("Nothng."). 1 of 73 quotes not an exact substring (model inserted "he"). Feedback type overlaps BMW's label on 28/39 labelled verbatims; most of the 11 mismatches are BMW "Difficult to Use" on things that are actually faults (CarPlay drops, trunk opening by itself), where our label looks more accurate. Real errors: "seats less comfortable than expected" → `defect`, trunk opening → category Interior. BMW's own label was wrong on G60-0877 (says trunk light, text is about vanity mirror).
- **Derivation:** 5 requirements, every cited ID exists, all have evidence (2–9 verbatims each); spot-checked citations support the claims. Weak points: all 5 tagged `at_successor_launch`, 4/5 Kano `basic`; metrics have no numeric targets (model says so in assumptions); 2 requirements rest on 2–3 verbatims, expected at n=50.
- **Re-estimate (D-014):** extraction ≈ $0.0009 per 25-verbatim call → ≈ $0.36 per full 10.1k run, ≈ $1.1 for 3 runs (plan $1.4). Derivation output was ~420 tokens/requirement vs 6k planned, but real input depends on the findings step (not built), so the derivation estimate stays as is. Plan total unchanged at ≈ $60.
- Prompt caching wrote almost the whole prompt on every call (+25% input, ~8% of pilot cost) with no reuse → Q-018.
- Follow-ups → Q-018. Source D finding → Q-005, `data-inventory.md`.

## G60 extraction results (2026-10-10, extract-v2, `bmw_req.pipeline.run_extract`)

- 160 luna Flex calls (2 validation + 158 full), 16 workers, 12 min; **$0.1348** ($0.00084/call); 421k in / 455k out (58k reasoning); 0 cache writes; 0 failed, 0 missing, 0 invented IDs; no retries needed.
- 4,000 verbatims → 3,732 in scope → **5,400 signals** (US 4,607 · RoW 485 · EU 308).
- Feedback types: like 2,777 · complaint 851 · want 699 · defect 580 · difficult_to_use 493.
- Top categories: Infotainment & Digital 1,023 · Driving Experience 901 · Comfort & Space 781 · Interior 572 · Exterior 550.
- 33 signals (0.6%) have unverified quotes — mostly stitched with "…" or a changed word form ("enjoy" vs "enjoys"); flagged, not dropped.
- Out-of-scope verdicts drop some usable content → Q-019 → re-check below.

## Q-019 re-check results (2026-10-10, `bmw_req.pipeline.recheck`, sol low, Flex)

- 11 calls, **$0.1342** (agent had estimated ≈ $0.05 — off by 2.7×: sol output 1.2–2k tokens/call at $5/M Flex). Avg 3.4k in / 1.6k out per call.
- First attempt: 7 of 11 batches refused by the run's own $0.30 cap, because the cap counts open reservations and each sol call reserves ≈ $0.13 worst case (4 in flight ≈ $0.53). No API calls were made for them; re-run with a $1 cap finished them. Lesson: size run caps to workers × worst-case reservation.
- **111 of 268 flipped to in scope, 157 confirmed out of scope; 118 new signals**, 0 unverified quotes, 0 missing IDs.
- New signals: difficult_to_use 80 (66 of them hotline questions like "customer asked which regen setting to use"), like 17, defect 12, complaint 5, want 4. Real recoveries include "only fast charged to 80%, which i really hated", a flat-tire defect, oil-dipstick want, removed gesture control. The question-type ones are a looser rule than the first pass applied → Q-020.
- G60 now: 3,843 in-scope verbatims, **5,518 signals**.
- Re-estimate: extraction for all 10.1k verbatims ≈ $0.34/run, below D-014's $0.47/run.

Update the budget table after every paid run. Once the app exists, the source of truth is the wrapper's usage log.

## Risks / watch-outs

- Local anaconda Python 3.9 has a broken pandas/numpy → use `uv venv --python 3.12`.
- Option lists are German-market only — the US/CN equipment baseline is an assumption.
- Plant capacity/flexibility is rarely public → feasibility checks need explicit assumptions (Q-011).
- BMW says engineering is out of scope → keep feasibility framed as a filter (Q-010).
- BMW data must never be committed or sent anywhere except OpenAI (AGENTS rule 1).
- Public sales are only in model-series pairs, with no regional per-model figures. Model-level market volume relies on BMW's `sales_volumes.xlsx`, which looks stylized and conflicts with public China data (Q-015).
- Scoring as drafted penalizes CN (no verbatims) and G70 EU (~19 verbatims) — see Q-004.
- Feedback data has no dates → the 2-year process must be demoed as simulated ingest waves (Q-012).
- `gpt-6-luna` structured-output quality is untested → pilot first (D-014); fallback `gpt-5-mini`.
- China-built i5 (G68 BEV) reportedly ended Jul 2026 (insider rumour, unconfirmed by BMW as of 2026-10-10) — affects 5 Series China powertrain assumptions.
- X5/7 Series successors: BMW calls them NK models, trade press says the platform is CLAR-derived (`bmw-annual-report-2025.md` §4). This matters for the G70 successor.

- 2026-10-10 — Foundation review (fresh session): data inventory re-verified (unique-ID counts, Source D/A reinterpretation, no study sample sizes, sales file conflict); brief gaps added; 23 web facts spot-checked and corrected; Q-004/005/006/010/012/013 updated, Q-015/016 added; consistency fixes. No code, no commit.
- 2026-10-10 — Budget re-baselined (D-014). BMW Group Report 2025 extracted (`documents/bmw-annual-report-2025.md`, page-cited); `portfolio-reference.md` upgraded to primary sources. No code, no commit.
- 2026-10-10 — Decision hygiene: undecided stack items reworded as Q-014 candidates (tech-stack, D-010 note, STATE, Q-002, README, knowledge-base). Usability: decision index, lighter session-start read list, glossary, fresh-clone setup, team/logistics placeholders, proposed demo path, duplicates removed. No code, no commit.
- 2026-10-10 — Atahan approved the stack table → D-015–D-020, Q-014 resolved, Q-017 opened. Scaffold: pyproject/uv, `src/bmw_req` (config, SQLite + sqlite-vec, budget-guarded OpenAI wrapper per D-014), Streamlit budget page, 12 tests passing. No paid calls, no commit.
- 2026-10-10 — Scaffold committed (65d3952). Q-017 delegated → D-021: demo slice G60 × US + G68 × CN, demo schema (audit append-only via triggers, sqlite-vec, llm_cache), G60 feedback ingest (4,000 verbatims, verified vs. inventory). 16 tests passing. No paid calls.

Q-018 → D-022 (extract-v2: `complaint` type, category definitions, quote check, no implicit cache writes; `signal`/`verbatim_extraction` tables; parallel runner). Full G60 extraction: 5,400 signals, $0.1348, 0 failures. Total spent $0.1549. Q-019 opened (out-of-scope over-exclusion). Not committed.

# Open Questions

Format: `Q-xxx` · owner · blocking? · context · options/recommendation. When resolved, move to "Resolved" with the answer + linked decision.

## Open

### Q-005 — How are the "Source A–D" feedback channels interpreted?
- Owner: team (ask BMW mentors)
- Context: Sources are anonymized. Observed patterns (`documents/data-inventory.md` §1) are hypotheses only:
  - **A:** multi-country (incl. JP/KR), lower-case normalized, possibly translated.
  - **B:** US only, third-person "Customer stated…" notes.
  - **C:** US only, structured survey prompts ("I had a minor/serious problem…", "What is…"), mostly Difficult-to-Use/Defect.
  - **D:** US only; short; unclassified. Two prompt templates in G60 (checked 2026-10-10): 34 of 136 end with "That is the one thing could be most improved about the <area> of my vehicle" (improvement answers, e.g. "the head rests are too short"); the rest are mostly "love the…" answers. So D mixes "what do you like" and "what could be most improved" — the earlier note that D is **not** improvement feedback was wrong.
- This affects source-trust weighting. Don't weight sources differently until confirmed.

### Q-006 — Customer study scales
- Owner: team (ask BMW mentors)
- Context:
  - The CN_EU sheet has numeric means in the range ~6.5–9.9 (0–10 or 1–10?).
  - The US sheet is a 7-point distribution ("I Hate It" … "I Love It").
  - **Neither sheet has sample sizes** — ask for n per model/market.
- Needed to compare/normalize, and to judge whether differences are meaningful.

### Q-007 — Team roles & who is the "PM" in the demo?
- Owner: team

### Q-008 — Hackathon logistics
- Owner: team
- Questions: submission deadline, demo length, required format (video/live/slides), judging criteria.

### Q-011 — How detailed can plant/platform reference data be?
- Owner: team
- Context: public sources give plant ↔ model/platform mapping and NK timing, rarely capacity or flexibility. Decide what granularity we claim, and mark the rest as assumptions.

### Q-013 — Market profile sources
- Owner: team
- Context: D-011 needs climate/usage/culture per market. Use research agents + cited sources (mobility studies, climate data, J.D. Power China/US).
- How deep do we go? EU as one market or split (DE vs. GB vs. Nordics)? Note that F70 feedback is 32% Japan and G60/G70 have KR/JP feedback (RoW).
- Recommendation: EU / US / CN (+ RoW where data exists) for the demo; the data model already supports countries.

### Q-015 — Are the BMW sales volumes real or illustrative?
- Owner: team (ask BMW mentors)
- Context: `sales_volumes.xlsx` conflicts with public data:
  - Its values are round thousands (all but one).
  - G60/G68 China is 68k → 75k (+10%) for 2024 → 2025, while public figures say 5 Series China (China-built, CPCA) Jan–Nov 2025 = 107,348 and BMW+MINI China fell 12.5%.
  - F70 EU 85k vs. 1 Series Europe 91,931 (Dataforce).
  - There is no powertrain split, although the briefing promised one.
- Also: F70 China 2024 is a formula cell (`=-D3-C10`, value 0) — another sign the file was constructed (2026-10-10).
- Until answered: use the file as BMW-internal relative weights, don't blend it with public figures, and show the conflict (`data-inventory.md` §3, `portfolio-reference.md` §4).

### Q-016 — Is driver assistance (ADAS) in scope?
- Owner: team (ask BMW mentors)
- Context:
  - BMW's process image (image_2) lists *Driver assistance* and *Powertrain* as requirement groups.
  - ADAS is a top purchase driver in China (`competitor-landscape.md` §2).
  - But "safety" is out of scope (regulatory).
- Working line (not decided): ADAS *experience* (usability, availability, comfort, trust) is in; safety/homologation performance is out.

## Resolved

# Challenge Brief — BMW "AI for Product Decision Making"

Source: `challange information document/BMW_Hackathon_Briefing_Short.pdf`, `mission.md`, `image_1.png`, `image_2.png`, `data_and_source.png`.

## The question

> What should the next generation of a BMW vehicle offer its customers?

Build an AI-powered app that helps **product managers (PMs)** derive, justify and prioritize **customer requirements** for a **successor vehicle**, grounded in customer feedback, BMW product + sales data, and web research — with the **PM firmly in control of every decision**.

Why (PDF): turning large volumes of feedback, market signals, competitor info and product data into requirements is today "largely manual, time-consuming, and difficult to trace consistently".

- Vehicles: BMW **1 Series (F70)**, **5 Series (G60, China LWB = G68)**, **7 Series (G70)** — any one or a combination. (The PDF says only "1/5/7 Series"; the e-codes come from the data files.)
- Markets: **Europe, China, US** — any subset.
- **Minimum:** demonstrate at least **one derivative in one market**, but don't design a one-off; it must be adaptable to other vehicles/markets. The remaining datasets/scenarios are *optional* testing material (mission.md).
- Horizon: **3–5 years ahead** (needs at successor launch, not just today).
- Definition: **Customer Requirement = Customer-relevant attribute of a car.**
- Must make clear **what is evidence vs. forward-looking assumption**.

## The app must be able to

1. **Ingest** provided data and **enrich** with structured web knowledge.
2. **Extract signals** — recurring complaints, unmet needs, competitor advantages, market trends — **each linked to sources**.
3. **Derive requirements** — clear, actionable, customer-facing, realistic.
4. **Prioritize** — with a logic we define and can explain.
5. **Involve the PM** — approve, reject, edit, or challenge requirements, rationale and evidence.
6. **Audit trail** — complete chronological record of all actions, changes, access events.

## Scope

**In:** features, equipment, comfort, space, usability, infotainment & digital services, design & quality perception, driving experience, range & charging *as experienced by the customer*, variant & package offering.

**Out:** regulatory/homologation (safety, emissions, type approval); technical/engineering (component specs, architecture, suppliers); pricing / business case / cost calculation (rough cost/effort as a prioritization factor is OK).

### Scope tensions (unresolved — don't paper over them)

- **Platform/plant feasibility vs. "architecture" out of scope.** BMW's out-of-scope list names "architecture". Vehicle platforms (CLAR, FAAR, NK) arguably *are* that. D-009 uses platform/plant data as a feasibility gate, which is our addition and not asked for by BMW. It also rests mostly on trade-press reference data. Open with BMW mentors: Q-010.
- **Driver assistance vs. "safety" out of scope.** BMW's own process image lists *Driver assistance* (and *Powertrain*) as requirement groups, and ADAS-as-experienced is a top purchase driver in China. But safety requirements are out of scope. Our working line: ADAS *experience* (usability, availability, comfort) is in; safety/homologation performance is out. Open: Q-016.
- **"Business" prioritization dimension vs. no business case.** image_2 shows *Customer* and *Business* dimensions. We use market volume and rough effort only — no pricing or business-case math.

## Expected deliverables (checklist)

- [ ] **Concept + demonstrable prototype** — heterogeneous inputs → derived requirements → prioritization → human review.
- [ ] **Structured sample requirement list**. Each requirement has:
  - [ ] unique ID
  - [ ] clear, actionable description
  - [ ] linked findings and sources
  - [ ] priority / score
  - [ ] applied prioritization rationale
  - [ ] evidence level
  - [ ] key future-facing assumptions & uncertainties
  - [ ] current decision status
- [ ] **End-to-end workflow definition** — what AI does autonomously, where human review is mandatory.
- [ ] **Demonstrable audit trail** — requirement traceable from sources → findings → consolidation → scoring → prioritization → human decision; records changes to content, scores, priorities, evidence, status, with **who/what**, **when**, **rationale**.

The PDF ("What to demonstrate") phrases the same as three items:
1. **Concept and working prototype**: AI supports identification, formulation and prioritization of customer-facing requirements from the provided data and, where relevant, external sources.
2. **Representative set of requirements with clear evidence and reasoning**: show how feedback, product data, market signals or competitor insights become requirements, and explain what drives their priority.
3. **Transparent decision-support experience**: PMs can **review, challenge, modify, approve or reject** AI proposals. Evidence, assumptions, uncertainties and key decisions stay visible and traceable.

Freedom of approach:
- Teams choose the technical approach, architecture, prioritization logic and UX.
- Deliverables may be one integrated solution or connected concepts, prototypes, models and visualizations (mission.md).
- BMW is interested in how the solution turns information into insight and makes reasoning transparent, "**not in a specific workflow or technical architecture**" (PDF). → Don't over-invest in architecture at the expense of the demo.

## BMW's reference process (image_2.png)

1. **Situation analysis** — baseline (previous BMW model, BMW portfolio, sales volume; AI + human) + competition, customer/public feedback, product & global trends (AI).
2. **Structure & context** — classify, cluster, contextualize: AI standardizes findings, identifies duplicates, groups themes, connects insights → list of all potential requirements (0/1: implement?), e.g. BEV powertrain, cooler, seat ventilation. (AI)
3. **Requirements definition** — specification & quantification: measurable targets + acceptance criteria (e.g. "Range: 600 or 700 mi?", "Cooler for how many bottles?", "Seat ventilation: fast enough?"), grouped by Exterior / Interior / Powertrain / Driver assistance / … (AI + human)
4. **Prioritization** — Customer, Business, … dimensions. (AI + human)
5. **Documentation** — requirements tracking (shown as a cycle). (AI)

## Provided data, promised vs. delivered (`data_and_source.png`)

| Dataset | BMW says | Reality (see `data-inventory.md`) |
|---|---|---|
| Customer verbatims | free text on the current vehicle → pain points, unmet needs, must-not-lose | ✓; no China verbatims, no dates |
| Equipment list | standard/optional equipment "by trim and market" | German price lists only |
| Sales volumes | units "by powertrain and region" | region only, no powertrain; values look stylized (Q-015) |
| Customer study | ratings in various categories | ✓; CN/EU means vs. US 7-point distributions, no sample sizes |

## Judging signals (what BMW says it values)

- Trustworthy sources, transparent reasoning.
- Thoughtful prioritization.
- Clear handling of **uncertainty and conflicting evidence**.
- Customer value over engineering specs / regulation / business case.
- **Scalability** across vehicle lines, markets, future decisions → **don't build a one-off**.
- Focus is free: go deep where we're strongest, but show how it connects to the full path evidence → PM decision.

## BMW mentor clarifications (Discord, 2026-10-10)

Common PM pain points from BMW. **This is a paraphrase** — TODO: paste the verbatim Discord message (author, timestamp) here so the source is traceable.

1. **Balancing customer requirements across markets/regions.** Preferences differ by **climate, real-world usage and culture** — what works in one market can fail in another. → Never treat "the customer" as one group (D-011).
2. **Getting early customer feedback and extracting *future* requirements**, e.g. from feedback on predecessor vehicles. → Project what customers will want at successor launch, not just what they complained about (D-012).
3. **The requirements process is ongoing (~2 years), not a one-time list.** The most relevant requirements are re-prioritized again and again. → Continuous re-prioritization with history, so the PM sees how and why priorities changed (D-013).
4. *(BMW support, 2026-10-10)* **Use the BMW Group Report 2025** to ground ideas: (a) market & sales data (regional growth, deliveries by model series, EV adoption) for personas, demand and impact; (b) product strategy & R&D (R&D priorities, ConnectedDrive/My BMW App, NEUE KLASSE) to show alignment with BMW's investments and future architecture. → Extract in `bmw-annual-report-2025.md`. Note: alignment with BMW strategy is context for prioritization, not engineering output (scope).

"""PM-facing actions (the only write path the UI uses). Every action is a human action with a rationale and
an append-only audit event (AGENTS rules 5, 6, 8; D-003, D-013).

Status machine: proposed → approved | rejected | deferred | challenged; challenged → (AI answers) → PM decides.
Only humans change status. Brand-fit `fail` blocks approval unless the PM overrides with a rationale.
"""

import json
import sqlite3

from bmw_req.pipeline.requirements import audit

HUMAN_STATUSES = {"approved", "rejected", "deferred", "challenged", "proposed"}
EDITABLE = ["title", "description", "category", "target_metric", "acceptance_criteria", "horizon", "kano_class",
            "kano_drift", "assumptions", "uncertainties", "conflicting_evidence", "effort"]
PRIORITIES = ["Must", "Should", "Could"]


class ActionError(ValueError):
    pass


def _need(actor: str, rationale: str):
    if not actor or not actor.strip():
        raise ActionError("A named human actor is required.")
    if not rationale or len(rationale.strip()) < 5:
        raise ActionError("A rationale is required for every PM decision.")


def _tx(conn):
    conn.execute("BEGIN IMMEDIATE")


def log_access(conn: sqlite3.Connection, actor: str, action: str, entity_type: str, entity_id: str, detail=None):
    """Access events (view/export) are part of the audit trail (brief: 'all actions, changes, access events')."""
    audit(conn, actor_type="human", actor_id=actor or "anonymous", action=action, entity_type=entity_type,
          entity_id=entity_id, new=detail)


def brand_blocked(conn, req_id: str) -> list[str]:
    """Targets whose brand check failed and have no PM override."""
    fails = [f"{r['vehicle_model_id']}×{r['market_code']}" for r in conn.execute(
        """SELECT DISTINCT vehicle_model_id, market_code FROM fit_check f WHERE requirement_id = ? AND check_type = 'brand'
           AND result = 'fail' AND id = (SELECT MAX(id) FROM fit_check g WHERE g.requirement_id = f.requirement_id
           AND g.vehicle_model_id = f.vehicle_model_id AND g.market_code = f.market_code AND g.check_type = 'brand')""",
        (req_id,))]
    overridden = {r["entity_id"].split(":", 1)[1] for r in conn.execute(
        "SELECT entity_id FROM audit_event WHERE action = 'override_gate' AND entity_id LIKE ?", (f"{req_id}:%",))}
    return [t for t in fails if t not in overridden]


def set_status(conn, req_id: str, status: str, actor: str, rationale: str) -> None:
    _need(actor, rationale)
    if status not in HUMAN_STATUSES:
        raise ActionError(f"Unknown status {status}")
    req = conn.execute("SELECT status FROM requirement WHERE id = ?", (req_id,)).fetchone()
    if req is None:
        raise ActionError(f"No requirement {req_id}")
    if status == "approved":
        blocked = brand_blocked(conn, req_id)
        if blocked:
            raise ActionError(f"Brand-fit FAIL on {', '.join(blocked)} — override the gate with a rationale first.")
    _tx(conn)
    try:
        conn.execute("UPDATE requirement SET status = ? WHERE id = ?", (status, req_id))
        audit(conn, actor_type="human", actor_id=actor, action="set_status", entity_type="requirement",
              entity_id=req_id, field="status", old=req["status"], new=status, rationale=rationale)
        conn.execute("COMMIT")
    except BaseException:
        conn.execute("ROLLBACK")
        raise


def override_gate(conn, req_id: str, target: str, actor: str, rationale: str) -> None:
    _need(actor, rationale)
    _tx(conn)
    try:
        audit(conn, actor_type="human", actor_id=actor, action="override_gate", entity_type="requirement_target",
              entity_id=f"{req_id}:{target}", field="brand_fit", old="fail", new="overridden", rationale=rationale)
        conn.execute("COMMIT")
    except BaseException:
        conn.execute("ROLLBACK")
        raise


def set_priority(conn, req_id: str, vehicle: str, market: str, priority: str | None, actor: str, rationale: str) -> None:
    """PM confirms (or changes) the priority of one target."""
    _need(actor, rationale)
    if priority is not None and priority not in PRIORITIES:
        raise ActionError(f"Priority must be one of {PRIORITIES}")
    row = conn.execute("SELECT priority FROM requirement_target WHERE requirement_id = ? AND vehicle_model_id = ? AND market_code = ?",
                       (req_id, vehicle, market)).fetchone()
    if row is None:
        raise ActionError(f"{req_id} has no target {vehicle}×{market}")
    _tx(conn)
    try:
        conn.execute("UPDATE requirement_target SET priority = ? WHERE requirement_id = ? AND vehicle_model_id = ? AND market_code = ?",
                     (priority, req_id, vehicle, market))
        audit(conn, actor_type="human", actor_id=actor, action="set_priority", entity_type="requirement_target",
              entity_id=f"{req_id}:{vehicle}×{market}", field="priority", old=row["priority"] if row else None,
              new=priority, rationale=rationale)
        conn.execute("COMMIT")
    except BaseException:
        conn.execute("ROLLBACK")
        raise


def edit_requirement(conn, req_id: str, changes: dict, actor: str, rationale: str, *, actor_type: str = "human",
                     model: str | None = None) -> int:
    """Edit content fields; bumps version; one audit event per changed field. Returns the new version."""
    _need(actor, rationale)
    cur = dict(conn.execute("SELECT * FROM requirement WHERE id = ?", (req_id,)).fetchone())
    diff = {k: v for k, v in changes.items() if k in EDITABLE and v != cur.get(k)}
    if not diff:
        return cur["version"]
    _tx(conn)
    try:
        sets = ", ".join(f"{k} = ?" for k in diff)
        conn.execute(f"UPDATE requirement SET {sets}, version = version + 1 WHERE id = ?", (*diff.values(), req_id))
        for k, v in diff.items():
            audit(conn, actor_type=actor_type, actor_id=actor, action="edit", entity_type="requirement", entity_id=req_id,
                  field=k, old=cur.get(k), new=v, rationale=rationale, model=model)
        if cur["status"] == "approved" and actor_type == "human":
            pass   # an approved requirement stays approved after a PM edit; the edit is in the trail
        conn.execute("COMMIT")
    except BaseException:
        conn.execute("ROLLBACK")
        raise
    return cur["version"] + 1


def set_finding_link(conn, req_id: str, finding_id: int, relation: str | None, actor: str, rationale: str) -> None:
    """PM adds/removes/changes an evidence link (relation None = remove)."""
    _need(actor, rationale)
    old = conn.execute("SELECT relation FROM requirement_finding WHERE requirement_id = ? AND finding_id = ?",
                       (req_id, finding_id)).fetchone()
    _tx(conn)
    try:
        if relation is None:
            conn.execute("DELETE FROM requirement_finding WHERE requirement_id = ? AND finding_id = ?", (req_id, finding_id))
        else:
            conn.execute("INSERT OR REPLACE INTO requirement_finding (requirement_id, finding_id, relation) VALUES (?, ?, ?)",
                         (req_id, finding_id, relation))
        audit(conn, actor_type="human", actor_id=actor, action="edit_evidence", entity_type="requirement",
              entity_id=req_id, field=f"finding:{finding_id}", old=old["relation"] if old else None, new=relation,
              rationale=rationale)
        conn.execute("COMMIT")
    except BaseException:
        conn.execute("ROLLBACK")
        raise


def decide_proposal(conn, proposal_id: int, accept: bool, actor: str, rationale: str) -> None:
    """Accept or reject an AI change proposal. Accepting applies it (priority / content / link / new requirement)."""
    _need(actor, rationale)
    row = conn.execute("SELECT * FROM change_proposal WHERE id = ?", (proposal_id,)).fetchone()
    if row is None:
        raise ActionError(f"No change proposal {proposal_id}")
    p = dict(row)
    if p["status"] != "open":
        raise ActionError(f"Proposal {proposal_id} is {p['status']}")
    if accept:
        kind = p["kind"] or "priority"
        if kind == "priority":
            set_priority(conn, p["requirement_id"], p["vehicle_model_id"], p["market_code"], p["proposed_value"], actor,
                         f"Accepted AI proposal #{proposal_id}: {rationale}")
        elif kind == "content":
            edit_requirement(conn, p["requirement_id"], {p["field"]: p["proposed_value"]}, actor,
                             f"Accepted AI proposal #{proposal_id}: {rationale}")
        elif kind == "link_finding":
            set_finding_link(conn, p["requirement_id"], int(p["field"].split(":")[1]), p["proposed_value"], actor,
                             f"Accepted AI proposal #{proposal_id}: {rationale}")
        elif kind == "new_requirement":
            set_status(conn, p["requirement_id"], "proposed", actor, f"Accepted new AI requirement #{proposal_id}: {rationale}")
    _tx(conn)
    try:
        conn.execute("""UPDATE change_proposal SET status = ?, decided_by = ?, decided_at = strftime('%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%fZ','now'),
                        decision_rationale = ? WHERE id = ?""", ("accepted" if accept else "rejected", actor, rationale, proposal_id))
        audit(conn, actor_type="human", actor_id=actor, action="accept_proposal" if accept else "reject_proposal",
              entity_type="change_proposal", entity_id=str(proposal_id), field=p["field"], old=p["old_value"],
              new=p["proposed_value"], rationale=rationale)
        conn.execute("COMMIT")
    except BaseException:
        conn.execute("ROLLBACK")
        raise


def requirement_trail(conn, req_id: str) -> list[dict]:
    return [dict(r) for r in conn.execute(
        """SELECT * FROM audit_event WHERE (entity_type = 'requirement' AND entity_id = ?)
           OR (entity_type = 'requirement_target' AND entity_id LIKE ?)
           OR (entity_type = 'change_proposal' AND entity_id IN (SELECT CAST(id AS TEXT) FROM change_proposal WHERE requirement_id = ?))
           ORDER BY id""", (req_id, f"{req_id}:%", req_id))]


def export_requirements(conn) -> list[dict]:
    """Structured requirement list = the BMW deliverable (ID, description, findings+sources, score, rationale,
    evidence level, assumptions/uncertainties, status)."""
    out = []
    for r in conn.execute("SELECT * FROM requirement ORDER BY id"):
        r = dict(r)
        targets = [dict(t) for t in conn.execute("SELECT * FROM requirement_target WHERE requirement_id = ?", (r["id"],))]
        findings = []
        for f in conn.execute("""SELECT f.id, f.title, f.type, f.source_kind, f.vehicle_model_id, f.market_code, rf.relation
                                 FROM requirement_finding rf JOIN finding f ON f.id = rf.finding_id WHERE rf.requirement_id = ?""",
                              (r["id"],)):
            srcs = [dict(s) for s in conn.execute(
                """SELECT s.kind, s.ref, s.external_id, s.url, s.trust_tier, fs.quote FROM finding_source fs
                   JOIN source_item s ON s.id = fs.source_item_id WHERE fs.finding_id = ? LIMIT 25""", (f["id"],))]

            "conflicting_evidence": r["conflicting_evidence"],
            "targets": [{"target": f"{t['vehicle_model_id']}×{t['market_code']}", "realization": t["realization"],
                         "score": t["score"], "ai_proposed_priority": t["proposed_priority"],

                         "market_note": t["rationale"]}
                        for t in targets],

"""Save / restore named demo states of data/app.db (e.g. 'evidence', 'wave1', 'demo').

`uv run python scripts/demo_state.py save wave1`
`uv run python scripts/demo_state.py restore wave1`
`uv run python scripts/demo_state.py list`

Restore keeps the CURRENT llm_usage and llm_cache rows (the budget log must never lose spend, D-014, and cached
answers keep replays free). Snapshots live in data/snapshots/ (git-ignored). Stop the Streamlit app first.
"""

import shutil
import sqlite3
import sys

from bmw_req.config import get_settings
from bmw_req.db import connect

KEEP = ["llm_usage", "llm_cache"]


def snap_dir():
    d = get_settings().data_dir / "snapshots"
    d.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    return d


def save(name: str) -> None:
    src = connect()
    dst = sqlite3.connect(snap_dir() / f"{name}.db")
    src.backup(dst)
    dst.close()
    print("saved", snap_dir() / f"{name}.db")


def restore(name: str) -> None:
    path = snap_dir() / f"{name}.db"
    if not path.exists():
        raise SystemExit(f"no snapshot {name}")
    db = get_settings().db_path
    # 1) back up the tables we must keep to a file BEFORE touching the live DB (crash-safe)
    keep_file = snap_dir() / "_keep_llm.db"
    if keep_file.exists():
        keep_file.unlink()
    cur = connect()
    cur.execute(f"ATTACH DATABASE '{keep_file}' AS keep")
    for t in KEEP:
        cur.execute(f"CREATE TABLE keep.{t} AS SELECT * FROM main.{t}")
    cur.execute("DETACH DATABASE keep")
    cur.close()
    # 2) swap in the snapshot
    for suffix in ("-wal", "-shm"):
        p = db.with_name(db.name + suffix)
        if p.exists():
            p.unlink()
    shutil.copyfile(path, db)
    # 3) put the kept rows back (FKs off: signals etc. reference llm_usage ids that are re-inserted unchanged)
    conn = connect()
    conn.execute("PRAGMA foreign_keys=OFF")
    conn.execute(f"ATTACH DATABASE '{keep_file}' AS keep")
    conn.execute("BEGIN IMMEDIATE")
    for t in KEEP:
        conn.execute(f"DELETE FROM main.{t}")
        conn.execute(f"INSERT INTO main.{t} SELECT * FROM keep.{t}")
    conn.execute("""INSERT INTO audit_event (actor_type, actor_id, action, entity_type, entity_id, rationale)
                    VALUES ('system', 'demo_state', 'restore_snapshot', 'database', ?, 'Demo reset; LLM usage log kept')""",
                 (name,))
    conn.execute("COMMIT")
    conn.execute("DETACH DATABASE keep")
    conn.execute("PRAGMA foreign_keys=ON")
    print("restored", name, "(llm_usage / llm_cache kept; backup in", keep_file, ")")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    cmd = sys.argv[1] if len(sys.argv) > 1 else "list"
    if cmd == "save":
        save(sys.argv[2])
    elif cmd == "restore":
        restore(sys.argv[2])
    else:
        for p in sorted(snap_dir().glob("*.db")):
            print(p.stem, f"{p.stat().st_size / 1e6:.1f} MB")

input.command: cat src/bmw_req/pipeline/requirements.py
input.description: Read requirements pipeline

result.output:
"""Requirement derivation v2 (sol): findings → customer requirements with targets, evidence links,
horizon/Kano, assumptions and uncertainties (D-012, D-028).

`uv run python -m bmw_req.pipeline.requirements derive "5 Series" --wave 1 [--n 16] [--dry-run]`

Always incremental: the model sees the existing requirements of the line and only proposes requirements for
needs they don't cover yet (wave 1 starts empty). AI creates in status `proposed` only (AGENTS rule 5).
Every cited finding ID is validated; a draft without a valid supporting finding is dropped.
"""

import argparse
import json
import sqlite3
from typing import Literal

from pydantic import BaseModel, Field

from bmw_req.db import connect
from bmw_req.llm import LLM
from bmw_req.pipeline.extract import Category
from bmw_req.portfolio import LINES, SUCCESSOR_LAUNCH, TARGETS

PROMPT_VERSION = "derive-v6"
MAX_IMPROVE_FINDINGS = 110
MAX_LIKE_FINDINGS = 30


class TargetDraft(BaseModel):
    vehicle_model_id: str
    market_code: str
    realization: Literal["carry_over", "platform_wide", "derivative_specific", "market_variant", "package"]
    market_note: str = Field(description="Why this market needs it (or needs it differently); cite evidence or say 'assumption'")


class RequirementDraft(BaseModel):
    title: str = Field(description="≤ 12 words, customer-facing")
    description: str = Field(description="What the customer must be able to experience; solution-neutral where possible")
    category: Category
    target_metric: str = Field(description="Customer-perceivable measure with a proposed numeric target")
    acceptance_criteria: str
    horizon: Literal["today", "at_successor_launch"]
    horizon_reason: str
    kano_class: Literal["basic", "performance", "delighter"]
    kano_drift: str = Field(description="Expected Kano class at successor launch and why, or 'stable'")
    must_not_lose: bool = Field(description="True if this protects a praised strength rather than fixing a gap")
    effort: Literal["S", "M", "L"] = Field(description="Rough incremental effort vs. today's car: S = keep/protect, software, calibration, packaging; M = new content within an existing area; L = new hardware, package space or body change")
    effort_reason: str
    targets: list[TargetDraft]
    supporting_finding_ids: list[int]
    conflicting_finding_ids: list[int]
    conflicting_evidence: str = Field(description="Contradicting evidence and cross-market differences in plain language, or 'none found'")
    evidence_summary: str = Field(description="2–3 sentences: what the cited evidence shows, per market. Facts only")
    assumptions: list[str] = Field(description="Forward-looking beliefs (3–5 yr) incl. every proposed target value")
    uncertainties: list[str] = Field(description="What could make this wrong; evidence gaps")


class DerivationResult(BaseModel):
    requirements: list[RequirementDraft]


INSTRUCTIONS = """You are a senior BMW product-requirements analyst. You derive CUSTOMER REQUIREMENTS for the
SUCCESSOR of a BMW vehicle line (launch in 3–5 years) from evidence findings. A customer requirement is a
customer-relevant attribute of the car.

Input: the vehicle line, its derivatives and the target markets (derivative × market), market profiles,
brand guardrails, sales per target, existing requirements (already proposed — do NOT duplicate them),
and findings with IDs:
- verbatim findings: clustered customer feedback, with per-market counts (verbatims, share of that market's
  in-scope feedback, severity-weighted count). Markets differ: US, EU, RoW (Japan/Korea/Canada…) are separate
  customer groups. There are NO China verbatims.
- study findings: customer-study satisfaction items that are notably weak or strong for a model × market.
- web findings: cited competitor advantages, reviews, market trends, customer expectations per market.

Task: propose up to {n} NEW requirements — the most important customer needs the evidence supports that the
existing requirements don't cover. Prefer strong, multi-source needs; include must-not-lose strengths that a
successor could lose (e.g. through a new UI or platform); include forward-looking needs where web trends and
market evidence support them (e.g. China, where only study + web evidence exists).

Rules:
- Cite supporting_finding_ids (only IDs from the input; ≥ 1, ideally verbatim + study/web together). Cite
  conflicting_finding_ids and describe conflicts and cross-market differences — never hide them.
- Customer-facing only. No component specs, suppliers, architecture, regulatory/homologation or safety
  performance, no pricing/business case. Driver assistance only as experienced (usability, availability, trust).
- Solution-neutral where possible (the need, not the part), but concrete enough to act on.
- One customer need per requirement: do not bundle independent features (split them, or pick the strongest).
- target_metric: ONE primary customer-perceivable measure with a proposed numeric target (and per-line or
  per-market values where segments/markets differ). acceptance_criteria: how it is verified — the test method
  (e.g. customer clinic with N target customers, owner survey, defined road/climate test), the task set or
  conditions, and the pass threshold. Every target value is an assumption — list it in `assumptions`.
- targets: only from the allowed target list. Add a market ONLY if a cited finding for that market (verbatims
  there, a study item or web finding for it) supports the need, or the market profile makes it clearly
  relevant — then say so in market_note ("assumption: …"). Do not spread every requirement to every market:
  markets are different customers. Use `market_variant` or `package` when only some markets need it and
  `platform_wide` only for needs evidenced across markets.
- effort: rate the INCREMENTAL effort versus today's car. Protecting an existing strength or fixing software
  behaviour is S; most requirements are S or M; L only for new hardware, package space or body changes.
- Cover the spread of the evidence, in this order: (1) the largest pain points by severity-weighted count —
  every one of the ~10 biggest pain/want findings should be cited by some requirement unless out of scope;
  (2) must-not-lose strengths (at most a quarter of the requirements); (3) at least two requirements where the
  markets clearly differ (e.g. China-specific needs from study/web).
- Brand & segment fit: must fit BMW ("Sheer Driving Pleasure", driver focus, premium quality) and this segment.
- horizon: `today` = current shortcoming/strength, needed regardless of trends; `at_successor_launch` = the
  need grows or changes by launch. Kano: classify by today's reaction, drift in kano_drift.
- Separate evidence (evidence_summary) from assumptions. Do not invent numbers, quotes or facts."""


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- context
def _wave_metrics(metrics: dict, wave: int) -> dict:
    by = metrics.get("by_wave", {}).get(str(min(wave, 2)))
    return by or {"verbatims": 0, "markets": {}}


def visible_findings(conn: sqlite3.Connection, derivatives: list[str], wave: int) -> list[dict]:
    q = ",".join("?" * len(derivatives))
    rows = conn.execute(
        f"""SELECT * FROM finding WHERE (vehicle_model_id IN ({q}) OR vehicle_model_id IS NULL)
            AND COALESCE(first_wave, 1) <= ? ORDER BY id""",
        (*derivatives, wave),
    ).fetchall()
    return [dict(r) for r in rows]


def build_context(conn: sqlite3.Connection, line: str, wave: int) -> tuple[dict, set[int]]:
    derivs = LINES[line]["derivatives"]
    findings = visible_findings(conn, derivs, wave)
    allowed_ids: set[int] = set()

    verbatim, study, web = [], [], []
    for f in findings:
        m = json.loads(f["metrics_json"] or "{}")
        if f["source_kind"] == "verbatim":
            wm = _wave_metrics(m, wave)
            if wm["verbatims"] < 3:
                continue
            markets = {
                mk: {"verbatims": v["verbatims"], "share_pct": round(100 * (v["share"] or 0), 2),
                     "severity_weighted": v["severity_weighted"], "types": v["types"]}
                for mk, v in wm["markets"].items()
            }
            sw = sum(v["severity_weighted"] for v in wm["markets"].values())
            quotes = [r["quote"] for r in conn.execute(
                "SELECT quote FROM finding_source WHERE finding_id = ? AND quote IS NOT NULL LIMIT 2", (f["id"],))]
            verbatim.append({"id": f["id"], "new_in_this_wave": (f["first_wave"] or 1) == wave,
                             "derivative": f["vehicle_model_id"], "category": f["category"],
                             "type": f["type"], "title": f["title"], "summary": f["summary"],
                             "polarity": f["polarity"], "markets": markets, "_sw": sw, "example_quotes": quotes})
        elif f["source_kind"] == "study":
            if not m.get("notable"):
                continue   # average items reach requirements via the evidence linker, not derivation
            study.append({"id": f["id"], "new_in_this_wave": (f["first_wave"] or 1) == wave,
                          "derivative": f["vehicle_model_id"], "market": f["market_code"],
                          "type": f["type"], "title": f["title"], "summary": f["summary"]})
        elif f["source_kind"] == "web":
            web.append({"id": f["id"], "new_in_this_wave": (f["first_wave"] or 1) == wave,
                        "derivative": f["vehicle_model_id"], "market": f["market_code"],
                        "type": f["type"], "category": f["category"], "title": f["title"], "summary": f["summary"],
                        "sources": m.get("n_sources"), "tiers": m.get("tiers")})
    improve = sorted([v for v in verbatim if v["polarity"] != "like"], key=lambda v: -v["_sw"])[:MAX_IMPROVE_FINDINGS]
    likes = sorted([v for v in verbatim if v["polarity"] == "like"], key=lambda v: -v["_sw"])[:MAX_LIKE_FINDINGS]
    for v in improve + likes:
        v.pop("_sw")
    if wave == 1:   # everything is new in wave 1; the flag only matters for incremental waves
        for group in (improve, likes, study, web):
            for x in group:
                x.pop("new_in_this_wave", None)
    for group in (improve, likes, study, web):
        allowed_ids |= {x["id"] for x in group}

    targets = [{"derivative": d, "market": mk} for d in derivs for mk in TARGETS[d]]
    sales = {}
    for r in conn.execute(
        f"""SELECT s.vehicle_model_id, s.market_code, s.year, s.units FROM sales s JOIN source_item i ON i.id = s.source_item_id
            WHERE s.vehicle_model_id IN ({",".join("?" * len(derivs))}) AND i.wave <= ?""", (*derivs, wave)):
        sales.setdefault(f"{r['vehicle_model_id']}×{r['market_code']}", {})[r["year"]] = r["units"]
    markets = {r["code"]: {k: r[k] for k in ("name", "climate", "usage_patterns", "cultural_expectations",
                                              "infrastructure", "powertrain_mix") if r[k]}
               for r in conn.execute("SELECT * FROM market")}
    brand = conn.execute("SELECT positioning, core_values_json, guardrails_json FROM brand WHERE id = 'BMW'").fetchone()
    existing = [
        {"id": r["id"], "title": r["title"], "category": r["category"],
         "findings": [x[0] for x in conn.execute("SELECT finding_id FROM requirement_finding WHERE requirement_id = ?", (r["id"],))]}
        for r in conn.execute(
            f"""SELECT DISTINCT q.* FROM requirement q JOIN requirement_target t ON t.requirement_id = q.id
                WHERE t.vehicle_model_id IN ({",".join("?" * len(derivs))}) ORDER BY q.id""", derivs)
    ]
    ctx = {
        "vehicle_line": line, "segment": LINES[line]["segment"], "derivatives": derivs,
        "successor_launch": {d: SUCCESSOR_LAUNCH[d] for d in derivs},
        "allowed_targets": targets, "sales_units_bmw_internal_relative_only": sales,
        "market_profiles": markets,
        "brand": dict(brand) if brand else {"positioning": "Sheer Driving Pleasure; driver focus; premium quality"},
        "existing_requirements": existing,
        "verbatim_findings_improve": improve, "verbatim_findings_strengths": likes,
        "study_findings": study, "web_findings": web,
    }
    return ctx, allowed_ids


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- derive
INCREMENTAL = """

LATER WAVE: this is a re-run months later. Existing requirements already cover most needs. Propose a new
requirement ONLY if it is grounded in evidence marked new_in_this_wave=true (e.g. a newly arrived study gap or a
new competitor/market event) or in a large pain finding that no existing requirement cites. Do not restate or
slightly vary existing requirements. Returning fewer than {n} — or none — is correct when nothing new is needed."""


def derive(llm: LLM, ctx: dict, *, n: int, job: str, effort: str = "high", wave: int = 1) -> tuple[DerivationResult, object]:
    instructions = INSTRUCTIONS.format(n=n) + (INCREMENTAL.format(n=n) if wave > 1 else "")
    res = llm.generate(
        job=job, tier="smart", instructions=instructions,
        input=json.dumps(ctx, ensure_ascii=False, default=str), schema=DerivationResult,
        reasoning_effort=effort, max_output_tokens=40_000, flex=True,
    )
    return res.parsed, res


def validate(drafts: DerivationResult, allowed_ids: set[int], derivatives: list[str]) -> tuple[list, list[str]]:
    ok, problems = [], []
    allowed_targets = {(d, m) for d in derivatives for m in TARGETS[d]}
    for d in drafts.requirements:
        bad = [i for i in d.supporting_finding_ids + d.conflicting_finding_ids if i not in allowed_ids]
        if bad:
            problems.append(f"{d.title}: dropped unknown finding ids {bad}")
        d.supporting_finding_ids = [i for i in d.supporting_finding_ids if i in allowed_ids]
        d.conflicting_finding_ids = [i for i in d.conflicting_finding_ids if i in allowed_ids and i not in d.supporting_finding_ids]
        bad_t = [(t.vehicle_model_id, t.market_code) for t in d.targets if (t.vehicle_model_id, t.market_code) not in allowed_targets]
        if bad_t:
            problems.append(f"{d.title}: dropped invalid targets {bad_t}")
        seen, targets = set(), []
        for t in d.targets:
            key = (t.vehicle_model_id, t.market_code)
            if key in allowed_targets and key not in seen:
                seen.add(key)
                targets.append(t)
        d.targets = targets
        if not d.supporting_finding_ids or not d.targets:
            problems.append(f"{d.title}: DROPPED (no valid supporting finding or target)")
            continue
        ok.append(d)
    return ok, problems


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- portfolio merge
class MergeGroup(BaseModel):
    members: list[int] = Field(description="Indices of drafts (≥ 2, from different vehicle lines) that state the same customer need")
    title: str
    description: str
    target_metric: str
    acceptance_criteria: str
    reason: str


class MergeResult(BaseModel):
    groups: list[MergeGroup]


MERGE_INSTRUCTIONS = """You consolidate customer requirements for a BMW PORTFOLIO. Drafts come from separate vehicle
lines (1, 5, 7 Series). Group drafts that state the SAME customer need so it becomes one portfolio requirement
with targets on several derivatives (e.g. 'tactile everyday controls' in the 5 and 7 Series). Only group drafts
from different lines whose need and direction match — even if the numeric targets differ per segment (then
state targets per line). Also group drafts about the same need for different derivatives in one market (e.g.
China urban assistance for G68 and G70). Only needs that are genuinely segment-specific (e.g. luxury rear lounge
vs compact practicality) stay separate. For each group write a merged, segment-neutral title,
description, target metric and acceptance criteria (keep numeric targets; if they differ by segment, state
them per line). Return no groups if nothing matches."""


def lines_of(d: "RequirementDraft") -> str:
    from bmw_req.portfolio import line_of
    return " + ".join(sorted({line_of(t.vehicle_model_id) for t in d.targets}))


def consolidate(llm: LLM, drafts: list[tuple[str, RequirementDraft]], job: str) -> tuple[list[RequirementDraft], list[str]]:
    """drafts: [(line, draft)] → merged list. Union of targets, findings, assumptions; notes for the audit trail."""
    payload = [{"index": i, "line": line, "title": d.title, "category": d.category, "description": d.description,
                "target_metric": d.target_metric, "must_not_lose": d.must_not_lose}
               for i, (line, d) in enumerate(drafts)]
    res = llm.generate(job=job, tier="smart", instructions=MERGE_INSTRUCTIONS, input=json.dumps(payload, ensure_ascii=False),
                       schema=MergeResult, reasoning_effort="medium", max_output_tokens=16_000, flex=True)
    used, merged, notes = set(), [], []
    for g in res.parsed.groups:
        idx = [i for i in g.members if 0 <= i < len(drafts) and i not in used]
        if len({drafts[i][0] for i in idx}) < 2 and len(idx) < 2:
            continue
        used |= set(idx)
        base = drafts[idx[0]][1].model_copy(deep=True)
        others = [drafts[i][1] for i in idx[1:]]
        base.title, base.description = g.title, g.description
        base.target_metric, base.acceptance_criteria = g.target_metric, g.acceptance_criteria
        for o in others:
            base.targets += [t for t in o.targets if (t.vehicle_model_id, t.market_code) not in
                             {(x.vehicle_model_id, x.market_code) for x in base.targets}]
            base.supporting_finding_ids = sorted(set(base.supporting_finding_ids) | set(o.supporting_finding_ids))
            base.conflicting_finding_ids = sorted(set(base.conflicting_finding_ids) | set(o.conflicting_finding_ids))
            base.assumptions += [a for a in o.assumptions if a not in base.assumptions]
            base.uncertainties += [u for u in o.uncertainties if u not in base.uncertainties]
            base.evidence_summary += " " + o.evidence_summary
            if o.conflicting_evidence and o.conflicting_evidence.lower() != "none found":
                base.conflicting_evidence += " " + o.conflicting_evidence
            base.effort = max(base.effort, o.effort, key="SML".index)
            base.horizon = "at_successor_launch" if "at_successor_launch" in (base.horizon, o.horizon) else "today"
        lines = sorted({drafts[i][0] for i in idx})
        base.evidence_summary = f"[Portfolio requirement merged across {', '.join(lines)}: {g.reason}] " + base.evidence_summary
        merged.append(base)
        notes.append(f"merged {[drafts[i][1].title for i in idx]} → {g.title}")
    merged += [d for i, (_, d) in enumerate(drafts) if i not in used]
    return merged, notes


def next_req_id(conn: sqlite3.Connection) -> int:
    r = conn.execute("SELECT MAX(CAST(SUBSTR(id, 5) AS INTEGER)) FROM requirement").fetchone()[0]
    return (r or 0) + 1


def audit(conn, *, actor_type, actor_id, action, entity_type, entity_id, field=None, old=None, new=None,
          rationale=None, model=None, prompt_ref=None, run_id=None):
    conn.execute(
        """INSERT INTO audit_event (actor_type, actor_id, action, entity_type, entity_id, field, old_value, new_value,
                                    rationale, model, prompt_ref, run_id) VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?)""",
        (actor_type, actor_id, action, entity_type, entity_id, field,
         None if old is None else (old if isinstance(old, str) else json.dumps(old, ensure_ascii=False)),
         None if new is None else (new if isinstance(new, str) else json.dumps(new, ensure_ascii=False)),
         rationale, model, prompt_ref, run_id),
    )


def store(conn: sqlite3.Connection, drafts: list[RequirementDraft], *, model: str, usage_id: int | None,
          wave: int, run_id: int | None = None) -> list[str]:
    ids = []
    conn.execute("BEGIN IMMEDIATE")
    try:
        n = next_req_id(conn)
        for d in drafts:
            rid = f"REQ-{n:04d}"
            n += 1
            content = {
                "title": d.title, "description": d.description, "category": d.category,
                "target_metric": d.target_metric, "acceptance_criteria": d.acceptance_criteria,
                "horizon": d.horizon, "kano_class": d.kano_class, "kano_drift": d.kano_drift,
                "assumptions": "\n".join(f"- {a}" for a in d.assumptions),
                "uncertainties": "\n".join(f"- {u}" for u in d.uncertainties),
                "conflicting_evidence": d.conflicting_evidence, "effort": d.effort,
                "must_not_lose": int(d.must_not_lose),
            }
            conn.execute(
                """INSERT INTO requirement (id, title, description, category, target_metric, acceptance_criteria, horizon,
                       kano_class, kano_drift, assumptions, uncertainties, conflicting_evidence, status, version,
                       effort, must_not_lose, created_by, first_run_id, derivation_json)
                   VALUES (:id, :title, :description, :category, :target_metric, :acceptance_criteria, :horizon,
                       :kano_class, :kano_drift, :assumptions, :uncertainties, :conflicting_evidence, 'proposed', 1,
                       :effort, :must_not_lose, :created_by, :run_id, :derivation_json)""",
                {**content, "id": rid, "created_by": f"ai:{model}", "run_id": run_id,
                 "derivation_json": json.dumps({**d.model_dump(), "wave": wave, "llm_usage_id": usage_id,
                                                "prompt": PROMPT_VERSION}, ensure_ascii=False)},
            )
            audit(conn, actor_type="ai", actor_id="pipeline.requirements", action="create", entity_type="requirement",
                  entity_id=rid, new=content, rationale=d.evidence_summary, model=model, prompt_ref=PROMPT_VERSION,
                  run_id=run_id)
            for t in d.targets:
                conn.execute(
                    """INSERT INTO requirement_target (requirement_id, vehicle_model_id, market_code, realization, rationale)
                       VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, ?)""",
                    (rid, t.vehicle_model_id, t.market_code, t.realization, t.market_note),
                )
                audit(conn, actor_type="ai", actor_id="pipeline.requirements", action="add_target",
                      entity_type="requirement", entity_id=rid, field="target",
                      new={"target": f"{t.vehicle_model_id}×{t.market_code}", "realization": t.realization},
                      rationale=t.market_note, model=model, prompt_ref=PROMPT_VERSION, run_id=run_id)
            for fid, rel in [(f, "supports") for f in d.supporting_finding_ids] + [(f, "contradicts") for f in d.conflicting_finding_ids]:
                conn.execute("INSERT OR IGNORE INTO requirement_finding (requirement_id, finding_id, relation) VALUES (?, ?, ?)",
                             (rid, fid, rel))
            audit(conn, actor_type="ai", actor_id="pipeline.requirements", action="link_findings",
                  entity_type="requirement", entity_id=rid, field="evidence",
                  new={"supports": d.supporting_finding_ids, "contradicts": d.conflicting_finding_ids},
                  model=model, prompt_ref=PROMPT_VERSION, run_id=run_id)
            ids.append(rid)
        conn.execute("COMMIT")
    except BaseException:
        conn.execute("ROLLBACK")
        raise
    return ids


def main():
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    ap.add_argument("cmd", choices=["derive", "context"])
    ap.add_argument("line")
    ap.add_argument("--wave", type=int, default=1)
    ap.add_argument("--n", type=int, default=15)
    ap.add_argument("--effort", default="high")
    ap.add_argument("--dry-run", action="store_true")
    args = ap.parse_args()
    conn = connect()
    ctx, allowed = build_context(conn, args.line, args.wave)
    if args.cmd == "context":
        s = json.dumps(ctx, ensure_ascii=False, default=str)
        print(f"context: {len(s)} chars; improve {len(ctx['verbatim_findings_improve'])}, likes "
              f"{len(ctx['verbatim_findings_strengths'])}, study {len(ctx['study_findings'])}, web {len(ctx['web_findings'])}")
        return
    llm = LLM(conn=conn)
    result, res = derive(llm, ctx, n=args.n, job=f"derive:{args.line}:w{args.wave}", effort=args.effort, wave=args.wave)
    drafts, problems = validate(result, allowed, LINES[args.line]["derivatives"])
    print(f"cost ${res.cost_usd:.4f}; {len(result.requirements)} drafts, {len(drafts)} valid")
    for p in problems:
        print("  !", p)
    if args.dry_run:
        from bmw_req.config import get_settings
        out = get_settings().data_dir / "eval" / f"derive_dry_{args.line.replace(' ', '')}_w{args.wave}.json"
        out.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        out.write_text(json.dumps([d.model_dump() for d in drafts], indent=1, ensure_ascii=False))
        print("wrote", out)
        return
    print(store(conn, drafts, model=llm.model_for("smart"), usage_id=res.usage_id, wave=args.wave))


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
